signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads the G10 currency strength scorecard with a 1W average gain of +0.852% across its G10 pairs, while EUR ranks as the weakest laggard at -0.518% across 9 pairs, opening a 1.370% leader-to-laggard spread. Norges Bank maintains a restrictive policy stance with a 4.50% policy rate and a +1.82% real yield, compared to the ECB at 2.65% with a +0.30% real rate. ECB Governing Council accounts expected today are likely to reinforce concerns over slowing demand and persistent energy shocks as highlighted by ECB officials. EUR/NOK trades below model fair value with a BEER z-score of -2.48σ, while USD/NOK holds above its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster at 9.474, 9.424, and 9.552. Trade bias: Short EUR/NOK; monetary policy divergence and rate premium support continued NOK outperformance. Catalyst: ECB Monetary Policy Meeting Accounts release at 11:30 UTC today. Risk: A rebound in European growth indicators or a sharp drop in Brent crude below $85/bbl.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Bond Volatility & Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.21, holding above its SMA20 at 156.87 and SMA50 at 157.69 while remaining capped below the SMA200 at 158.51. Fed policy at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% generates a +267bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry advantage for USD, keeping underlying structural demand intact. Options market pricing reflects elevated downside hedging, with 1M 25d Risk Reversals printing a strong put skew of -1.94 alongside an implied volatility discount of 8.2% vs 30-day realized volatility of 9.9% (VRP -1.6%). Cross-asset indicators show elevated rate uncertainty, with the MOVE index at the 95th percentile of its trailing-year range while VIX sits at the 12th percentile (15.1). Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; persistent carry differential supports buying on dips near moving average support. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims and Fed Governor Waller speech at 12:30 UTC today. Risk: Verbal intervention from Japanese authorities or a sustained drop in US 10-year Treasury yields below 5.20%.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Stress + Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1198, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1404), SMA50 (1.1519), and SMA200 (1.1605) technical moving average cluster. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR at -82,445 contracts (pctl 6, z -1.65) after a WoW net reduction of -23,640 contracts, pointing to persistent institutional selling. The options market displays defensive pricing with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.7% vs 30-day realized volatility at 4.2%, creating a +2.5% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) alongside a -1.11 25d Risk Reversal put skew. Fed SOFR at 3.90% vs ECB €STR at 2.44% delivers a +146bp OIS yield advantage to USD, reinforced by US 5Y real yield gains of +53bp over the last 20 sessions (FRED). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; negative technical alignment and yield spreads weigh on spot performance. Catalyst: ECB Meeting Accounts at 11:30 UTC and US Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Hawkish shift in ECB accounts or a sharp drop in US Treasury yields.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT vs OIS Divergence + Retail Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4261, positioned above its SMA20 at 1.4085, SMA50 at 1.3968, and SMA200 at 1.3862. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net short position of -72,519 contracts (long% 23.8%, WoW -23,396) despite a +161bp OIS carry advantage for USD (SOFR 3.90% vs CORRA 2.29%) and a +175bp policy rate gap. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 92% short position, creating a contrarian divergence where retail traders are fading the broader USD uptrend. WTI crude oil rising +2.81% to $90.8/bbl provides near-term CAD support, conflicting with the wider monetary policy divergence. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD; institutional yield support and potential retail short squeeze favor upside continuation. Catalyst: Canada Employment Change and Unemployment Rate release at 12:30 UTC today. Risk: Canada labor data significantly beats expectations or WTI crude breaks above $95/bbl.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Support at Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3199, holding directly below its SMA20 (1.3324) and the closely aligned SMA50/SMA200 cluster at 1.3449 and 1.3442. Leveraged Funds positioning sits net short at -5,377 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.34) after a -11,896 WoW reduction, signaling stretched institutional positioning near multi-month lows. OIS carry slightly favors USD with SOFR at 3.90% vs SONIA at 3.73% (+17bp spread), while the BoE maintains a market bias toward further rate hikes compared to a neutral Fed stance. Options 25d Risk Reversals indicate a moderate put skew of -0.84 with implied volatility at 6.5% vs 30-day realized at 4.7% (+1.8% VRP). Trade bias: Neutral/Range GBP/USD; oversold speculative positioning neutralizes negative yield carry near key technical levels. Catalyst: BoE Governor Bailey speech at 12:15 UTC and BoE Credit Conditions Survey at 08:30 UTC. Risk: Dovish tone from Governor Bailey or a upside surprise in US jobless claims.
